title: Superstructure
headline: The building rises: blockwork, columns, lintels, beams and (for storey buildings) suspended slabs.
seoTitle: Blockwork, columns, lintels and slabs in Nigeria: superstructure guide
seoDescription: How blockwork, columns, lintels, beams and suspended slabs are built on Nigerian sites, what goes wrong, what to ask and what photos to request.
summary: Most of the cost and most of the structural risk sit here. Concrete and rods must match the engineer’s design.
duration: 4–10 weeks for a bungalow; each additional floor adds roughly 4–8 weeks [CHECK]
whatHappens: Blockwork: sandcrete blocks (9-inch external, 6-inch internal is common) laid in cement-sand mortar, typically 6–8 courses per day per gang so mortar can set. [CHECK local productivity]
Columns: reinforced concrete columns at corners and junctions in framed buildings, cast in formwork.
Lintels: reinforced concrete beams above doors and windows, or a continuous lintel band round the building.

Beams and suspended slabs (storey buildings): formwork and props, reinforcement fixed and checked, concrete poured and vibrated, props left in for the time the engineer specifies (often 14–21 days or more). [CHECK]
Wall plate / ring beam at the top of walls ready for the roof.
problems: Low-quality blocks (too much sand, not cured) that crumble — ask for block strength or test a sample.
Blockwork raised too fast in one day, causing walls to bulge or crack.
Columns cast with rods out of position, honeycombed concrete, or without vibration.
Props removed too early to reuse them elsewhere — slabs sag or crack.
Rods in slabs fewer or smaller than the drawing; inadequate cover (rods too close to the surface).
Concrete ‘ready-mix’ that is actually site-mixed at a weaker ratio, or water added to make it easier to place.
No engineer inspection before casting slabs.
questions: Where are the blocks from, and can I see a strength test or a sample block?
How many courses per day are you laying?
Has the engineer inspected the reinforcement before each casting? Can I have the inspection note?
What concrete grade or mix are you using for columns, beams and slabs, and is it vibrated?
When will the props be removed, and on whose instruction?
Are the lintels continuous or only over openings?
photoCheckpoints: Blocks on site, and a close-up of a broken block to see its quality.
Blockwork progress photos from the same spots every few days.
Column and beam reinforcement before casting, with a tape showing stirrup spacing.
Slab reinforcement before casting, with spacers/chairs visible and tape showing spacing; rod size close-up.
Video of concrete pour with vibrator in use.
Props under the slab, and the date they were removed.
